questions.question: What is a correlation ID?

options.text: A unique identifier passed through all services handling a request, enabling end-to-end tracing

questions.explanation: Correlation ID: unique ID generated at request entry, propagated through all services. Included in logs, traces, errors. Enables: finding all logs for one request across services, debugging distributed systems.

questions.question: Why are correlation IDs important in microservices?

options.text: To trace a single request across multiple services and correlate logs/events

questions.explanation: Microservices challenge: one user request touches many services. Without correlation ID, can't connect logs. With it: search by ID, see entire request flow, identify where failures occurred. Essential for debugging.

questions.question: Where should a correlation ID be generated?

options.text: At the entry point (API gateway, first service) if not already present in the request

questions.explanation: Generate at entry: API gateway or first service. If client provides one, use it (enables client-side correlation). If not, generate UUID. Never generate new ID mid-flow—defeats purpose.

questions.question: How is a correlation ID typically propagated between services?

options.text: HTTP headers (X-Correlation-ID, X-Request-ID) or message metadata

questions.explanation: Propagation: HTTP header (X-Correlation-ID, X-Request-ID, traceparent), message queue metadata, gRPC metadata. Each service: extract from incoming, include in outgoing, add to all logs.

questions.question: What is the relationship between correlation IDs and distributed tracing?

options.text: Correlation ID is a simpler form; distributed tracing (trace ID + span ID) provides richer context

questions.explanation: Correlation ID: single ID for request. Distributed tracing: trace ID (like correlation ID) + span IDs (each operation) + timing + relationships. Tracing is richer but more complex. Correlation ID is minimum viable.

questions.question: What should you include in logs along with the correlation ID?

options.text: Correlation ID, timestamp, service name, log level, and contextual data

questions.explanation: Structured log: {correlationId: 'abc', timestamp: '...', service: 'order-service', level: 'INFO', userId: 123, message: '...'}. Enables: filter by correlation ID, see timeline, identify service, understand context.

questions.question: What is the W3C Trace Context standard?

options.text: A standard for propagating trace context (including trace ID) across services via HTTP headers

questions.explanation: W3C Trace Context: standard headers (traceparent, tracestate) for distributed tracing. Enables interoperability between tracing systems. traceparent contains: version, trace-id, parent-id, flags. Widely adopted.

questions.question: How do you handle correlation IDs with asynchronous messaging?

options.text: Include correlation ID in message headers/metadata, extract and use in consumer
Generate new ID for each message

questions.explanation: Async messaging: include correlation ID in message metadata (Kafka headers, SQS attributes, RabbitMQ properties). Consumer extracts and uses for its logs. Maintains traceability across async boundaries.

questions.question: What is a common mistake with correlation IDs?

options.text: Generating a new ID in each service instead of propagating the original

questions.explanation: Common mistake: each service generates its own ID. Result: can't correlate logs across services. Correct: generate once at entry, propagate everywhere. Every service uses the same ID for the same request.

questions.question: How do correlation IDs help with error debugging?

options.text: Search logs by correlation ID to see entire request flow and identify where error occurred

questions.explanation: Error debugging: user reports error with correlation ID (shown in error page). Search logs: see request enter API gateway → service A → service B (error here). Pinpoint failure location, see context. Invaluable.

questions.question: Should correlation IDs be exposed to end users?

options.text: Yes, in error messages—helps support teams debug issues when users report problems

questions.explanation: Expose in errors: 'Error occurred. Reference: abc-123-def'. User provides to support. Support searches logs by ID. Much faster than 'it happened around 3pm'. Include in error responses, error pages.

questions.question: A user reports an error. Support can't find relevant logs among millions. What's missing?

options.text: Correlation IDs—without them, can't connect user's request to specific log entries

questions.explanation: Without correlation ID: search by time (too many results), user ID (still many requests), guess which logs are related. With correlation ID: one search, exact request, all services. Night and day difference.
